title: Blending sounds to read a new word
examples: How do I sound out a word?
How do I read a word I have never seen?

figure.name: x-word
figure.note: Say each sound, then push them together

explain.say: Imagine you meet a word you have never seen. No worries, you can solve it like a puzzle! Look at the first box on the board: f. It makes the sound fff, like air coming out of a tyre.

draw.text: Blending sounds to read a new word

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Say each sound, then push them together

explain.say: Now look at the next box: r. It says rrr, like a growling puppy. Say the two together slowly with me: fff, rrr. Can you feel your mouth slide from one sound to the next?

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Say each sound, then push them together

explain.say: The third box is lighting up: o. It says o, as in on. Now you have fff, rrr, o. Keep the sounds in a line, like train carriages joining up.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Say each sound, then push them together

explain.say: The last box is g, a quick sound from the back of your throat. Now say all four sounds faster and faster: f, r, o, g... frog! Pushing sounds together like that is called blending.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Say each sound, then push them together

explain.say: Well done, you just read a word by blending! The board has a longer word now. Say each sound: s, u, n, s, e, t. Blend them fast and you get sunset. Challenge: blend the sounds of your own name!

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Six sounds blend into one word

faq.a: Blending means saying the sounds in a word one after another and pushing them together until you hear the word. f, r, o, g becomes frog.

faq.q: What if my blended word sounds wrong?
faq.a: Say the sounds again a little faster and think of a word you know that sounds close. A few words, like said and the, do not follow the usual sounds, so we learn them by sight.
asks: Why does the word sound wrong when I blend it?

faq.q: What is the difference between a letter name and a letter sound?
faq.a: The name of f is eff, but its sound is fff. For blending you use the sound, otherwise frog would come out as eff, ar, oh, gee.

faq.q: How can I get faster at blending?
faq.a: Practise short words every day, like cat, sun, hop and pig. Run your finger under each letter as you say its sound, then sweep it fast as you say the whole word.
A CVC word has a consonant, then a vowel, then a consonant, like dog, map or bed. They are the first words most children learn to blend.

facts: English has about 44 sounds, called phonemes, but only 26 letters to write them.
In England, six-year-olds take a phonics check of 40 words, some of them made-up words, to test blending.
